To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of environmental pollutants on the induction of drug metabolism enzymes can be studied in cultured hepatocytes, and that these effects can be used to classify the pollutants according to their mode of action.

(i) we developed a new model of toxicity assessment based on P450 induction in hepatocyte cultures; (ii) we demonstrated that the use of three hepatocyte models (rat fetal, quail fetal, human adult) is more efficient than a single hepatocyte model for the evaluation of environmental pollutant toxicity; and (iii) the use of this model allows the classification of pesticides according to their mechanism of action and the identification of new P450 inducers.

the use of three different cell lines, namely rat fetal, quail fetal and HepG2 cells, in combination with a panel of pesticides allowed to identify different groups of inducers, which are likely to induce the expression of different CYP isoforms in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of cultured hepatocytes for the evaluation of environmental pollutant toxicity.
the study of environmental pollutants and the development of a predictive model of their toxicity.
the development of a predictive model for the evaluation of short-term toxicological effects of environmental pollutants on the hepatic P450 system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a panel of different cell types, each of which is sensitive to a specific type of inducer, is a valuable approach to the study of the effects of environmental pollutants.
lindane and pentachlorophenal induce the CYP3A family in human and quail cells and the CYP1A family in rat and quail cells, whereas dieldrin induces the CYP2B family in quail cells.
pentachlorophenoxy, lindane, and dieldrin are the strongest inducers, whereas the other pesticides are weak or noninducers of drug-metabolism enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a hierarchical cluster analysis of P450 induction in hepatocytes from different species is useful in identifying the mechanisms of action of environmental pollutants.
the current study results highlight advantages of using several types (fetal rat, adult quail, Hep G2) of cultured hepatocytes for the in vitro evaluation of short-term toxicity of pesticides.
the use of cultured cells from different origins is a useful tool to predict the potential toxicity of environmental pollutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of several types of cells in vitro is a useful tool for the prediction of the potential toxicity of environmental pollutants.
the induction of drug metabolizing enzymes in cultured hepatocytes is a useful approach for the evaluation of environmental pollutants.
the in vitro approach using different hepatocytes is a useful tool for predicting the in vivo toxicity of environmental pollutants.
